## Overview

With `--enable-dbo` and an all2all backend that reserves communication SMs (e.g. DeepEP high-throughput), DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) crash in the sparse-attention indexer as soon as a microbatched step contains a decode-branch request:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:346): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 and _meta_info_size == 2
```

The indexer builder plans DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits schedule for the whole GPU, but DBO lowers DeepGEMM's SM count (`set_num_sms(total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS)`) while the microbatches run. This PR re-plans the schedule at the call site when the two counts differ. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `schedule_meta_size`, `dbo indexer num_sms`, `paged_mqa_logits set_num_sms`: 0 results). Rechecked 2026-10-08 against open PRs: #56476 (DeepSeek-V4.1 per-microbatch index state) also edits `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, in different lines, and does not touch the schedule metadata.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSA indexer decode crash under DBO (Model Runner V1 and V2, CUDA + DeepGEMM).
- The re-planned schedule gives bit-identical indexer logits, so the fix does not change results: with it, GLM-5.3 accuracy under DBO matches DBO with SM partitioning disabled (`VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0`), where this code path never runs.
- Separately, GLM-5.3 accuracy with DBO on is well below DBO off (GSM8K ~0.6 vs 0.93) with or without this change. That is a separate, pre-existing DBO bug in GLM-5.x's shared top-k layers that this crash was hiding, fixed in #60734 (see Validation).
- No cost when the SM count is unchanged (one host-side `get_num_sms()` per indexer layer). Under DBO, one ~9 µs metadata kernel per microbatch per forward, reused by all indexer layers. No host syncs; CUDA-graph safe.
- XPU / ROCm paths unchanged.

## Validation

This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8; the rebase did not change the patch (same `git patch-id`). The unit and related tests below were re-run on the rebased commit (H200) with the same results. The GSM8K runs predate the rebase and used main @ 4a705c7b with and without this patch.

**Unit test (new)**, `tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_schedule_metadata.py`: plans a schedule for the full GPU, lowers DeepGEMM's SM count by 20 (what `create_sm_control_context` does), and checks that `get_schedule_metadata()` re-plans once, the kernel runs, and logits match the full-SM result on all valid columns; the original schedule comes back after the SM count is restored. Runs in the existing H100/B200 "V1 Attention" CI shards; skipped without DeepGEMM or below SM90.

| Build | GPU | Result |
|---|---|---|
| this branch (main @ 4a705c7b, precompiled from 2e06395f) | H200 | `next_n` 1, 2, 4: 3 passed |
| vLLM 0.29.0 + backport | H200 | `next_n` 1, 2: passed (`next_n=4` needs a newer DeepGEMM than 0.29 ships) |

Related existing tests on this branch (H200): `tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py` 5 passed, `test_indexer_native_next_n.py` 9 passed, `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` 7 passed, `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py` 114 passed, `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 292 passed (1,188 skipped by hardware). `test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`: 30 passed, 3 could not run locally (they load the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` config); they fail identically on main and do not touch the changed code.

**Kernel-level check** (H200, DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`, GLM-5.3 indexer shapes: 32 heads x 128, block 64, 13 requests with contexts 1 to 32k):

| SM count | Schedule planned for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 132 | 132 | reference |
| 112 (inside vLLM's `SMControlContextManager`) | 132 | the production assertion |
| 112 | 112 (this PR) | runs; logits bit-identical to the reference |

**End-to-end reproducer, before/after.** A 4-layer GLM-5.3 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, production attention/indexer geometry, dummy weights) on 2 x H200, DP2/EP2, `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 32 --dbo-decode-token-threshold 32`, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8_per_block + fp8 KV, prefix caching. Workload: random-token prompts of `64*k+1` tokens, then exact repeats (a full prefix-cache hit leaves a 1-token short extend at the head of the batch) mixed with fresh long prompts, pinned per DP rank. vLLM 0.29.0 with and without the backport of this patch (same two files):

| Run | DBO steps | Assertion | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off | 0 | 0 | 6 rounds, 0 errors |
| DBO on, without fix | 4 | yes, 6 s after the first DBO step | 29/32 failed in round 2, engine dead |
| DBO on, with fix | 28 | 0 | 6 rounds, 0 errors |
| DBO on, with fix, 30 rounds incl. decodes | 158 | 0 | 944 requests, 0 errors |

With the fix, DBO-on generations equal DBO-off: 944/944 identical sequences (7,440/7,440 tokens), first-token logprob difference at most 1.9e-6.

**Model evaluation, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, DeepEP high-throughput, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8 KV, prefix caching, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` as on our production prefill, FlashInfer prebuilt kernels; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`):

| vLLM | Config | GSM8K exact_match (flexible / strict) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | DBO off | 0.927 / 0.928 |
| main (without fix) | DBO on | crash: the assertion on 8 workers, 4 engines dead, eval aborted |
| this branch | DBO on | 0.592 / 0.582 (all 1,319 answered) |
| main (without fix) | DBO on, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` (fix path never runs) | 0.610 / 0.608 |
| this branch | DBO on, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.623 / 0.606 |
| 0.29.0 | DBO on | crash: the assertion on 8 workers, eval aborted |
| 0.29.0 + backport | DBO on | 0.669 / 0.681 (all 1,319 answered) |

The fix turns the crash into a completed eval. The drop from 0.93 to ~0.6 with DBO on is not caused by it: the `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` rows never re-plan (and never crash) and land in the same range. DBO with GLM-5.x has an accuracy bug of its own that this crash has been hiding: layers that reuse another layer's top-k read it from state shared across microbatches. #60734 fixes it; with both PRs, GLM-5.3 with DBO on scores 0.922 / 0.923 (DBO off: 0.927 / 0.928).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_schedule_metadata.py

# GSM8K
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8):
- `create_sm_control_context` (`vllm/v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py:83-126`) uses `deep_gemm.set_num_sms` as the compute-SM setter whenever `has_deep_gemm() and comm_sms > 0`, so inside the microbatches DeepGEMM sees `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` SMs (132 - 20 = 112 on H100/H200). It keys on DeepGEMM being importable, not on `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM`. `comm_sms` is 0 only for DeepEP low-latency and NIXL-EP.
- The context wraps the microbatched forward in both runners (`gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py:426,453`; MRV2 `gpu/ubatch_utils.py:496`), after attention metadata has been built.
- The indexer builder plans the decode schedule for `num_compute_units` SMs (`v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py:967-968`, `:1688-1697`, MTP drafts `:1782-1789`), and `sparse_attn_indexer.py:729` / `glm5next/nvidia/sparse_indexer.py:582` pass it to `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`, which asserts it against the current SM count.
- The decode branch takes every request with `query_len <= 1 + num_speculative_tokens`, including 1-token short extends of prefix-cached prompts, which the reorder puts first. A step is microbatched only when every DP rank votes for it.

**How it was found:** GLM-5.3 RL with P/D disaggregation; prefill DP32/EP32 with DeepEP high-throughput, DBO, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, prefix caching, vLLM 0.29.0 on H200. One prefill rank hit the assertion after ~28 h; the other 31 then timed out in DeepEP dispatch and failed with `torch.cat(): expected a non-empty list of Tensors`.

**Fix:** `DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata` records the SM count and block size the schedule was planned with. `get_schedule_metadata()` returns the planned schedule when DeepGEMM's current SM count matches; otherwise it re-plans with the same inputs and caches the result per SM count. The planned count is stored rather than derived from the tensor shape because SM90 `next_n=4` plans `num_sms // 2 + 1` schedule rows. `update_draft_decode_metadata` rewrites `seq_lens` in place, so it clears the cache. In FULL-graph DBO capture the re-plan kernel is captured and reads the persistent `seq_lens`/`indices` buffers; eager warmups under the same context JIT-compile it before capture.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Plan for the reduced SM count in the builder: the builder would need to replicate `create_sm_control_context` (all2all `max_sms_used()`, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS`, the ROCm override) for both runners, and anything else that changes DeepGEMM's SM count would break it again.
2. Skip `set_num_sms` in SM control: removes DBO's compute/communication SM partitioning for every DeepGEMM GEMM.
3. Re-plan inside the `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` wrapper: no per-forward object to cache on, so every indexer layer would re-plan.
4. Build both schedules up front: an extra kernel every step even when DBO does not split.
</details>

**Not affected:** the sparse-MQA schedule of DeepSeek-V4.1 (planned inside the forward), FlashMLA scheduler metadata, and prefill `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

why can not we build metadata based on `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` in the first place? Instead of changing it at forward time?

> why can not we build metadata based on `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` in the first place? Instead of changing it at forward time?

@zyongye  I considered that, so:
 - Whether a step is microbatched is only known per step, and the builder doesn't know. With --enable-dbo, DP ranks decide each step whether to split, and steps that don’t split run with all SMs. The microbatch-0 builder (get_metadata_builder(ubid or 0)) builds metadata for both split and unsplit steps, and build() gets no microbatch flag. A schedule planned for the reduced count up front would hit the same _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 assertion on every unsplit step. Doing it at build time would mean passing a “microbatched / compute SM count” argument from the runner into the builder, in both MRV1 and MRV2.
 
- The compute SM count actually isn’t just total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS. create_sm_control_context uses min(VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS, all2all_manager.max_sms_used()), forces 0 on ROCm with DeepEP HT, and only calls deep_gemm.set_num_sms when DeepGEMM is available and the comm SM count is > 0. The builder would need to duplicate that and stay in sync with it.

Re-planning at the call site uses the SM count DeepGEMM is actually running with (get_num_sms()), so it stays correct whichever code path changes it (The cost ofc is one small metadata kernel per microbatch, on the first indexer layer.)

Thanks for the reply. 

First of all, the metadata build is done at every engine step. The metadata don't reuse unless we explicitly cache them. 

> The microbatch-0 builder (get_metadata_builder(ubid or 0)) builds metadata for both split and unsplit steps, and build() gets no microbatch flag.

My sense is that for we can't get the exact SM count at metadata build time because the model runner is not exposed such value? 

If that's the case, I think this approach make sense to me. But I would double check if `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` implement caching already so we can save a lot of code in the engine.

3. Re-plan inside the `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` wrapper: no per-forward object to cache on, so every indexer layer would re-plan.
4. Build both schedules up front: an extra kernel every step even when DBO does not split.
</details>

**Not affected:** the sparse-MQA schedule of DeepSeek-V4.1 (planned inside the forward), FlashMLA scheduler metadata, and prefill `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The DSA indexer decode schedule must match DeepGEMM's current SM count.
+
+Dual-batch overlap lowers it (`deep_gemm.set_num_sms`) while microbatches run,
+after the metadata builder planned `schedule_metadata` for the whole GPU, and
+`fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` asserts the schedule matches the count in effect.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
+    fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits,
+    get_num_sms,
+    get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata,
+    native_next_n_supported,
+    set_num_sms,
+)
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_gemm
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA only")
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not has_deep_gemm(), reason="DeepGEMM not available")
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.has_device_capability(90), reason="SM90 and SM100 only"
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("next_n", [1, 2, 4])
+def test_decode_schedule_follows_deepgemm_num_sms(next_n: int):
+    if not native_next_n_supported(next_n):
+        pytest.skip(f"next_n={next_n} has no native kernel on this architecture")
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch_size, heads, head_dim, block_size, max_model_len = 4, 32, 128, 64, 2048
+    num_blocks = batch_size * max_model_len // block_size
+
+    q = torch.randn((batch_size, next_n, heads, head_dim), device="cuda")
+    weights = torch.randn((batch_size * next_n, heads), device="cuda")
+    # Fused FP8 cache: per block, the FP8 values then one fp32 scale per token.
+    kv = torch.randn((num_blocks, block_size, head_dim), device="cuda")
+    kv_scale = kv.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp(1e-4) / 448.0
+    kv_cache = torch.cat(
+        [
+            (kv / kv_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8).flatten(1),
+            kv_scale.view(torch.uint8).flatten(1),
+        ],
+        dim=1,
+    ).view(num_blocks, block_size, 1, head_dim + 4)
+    block_table = torch.randperm(num_blocks, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(
+        batch_size, -1
+    )
+    context_lens = torch.randint(
+        next_n, max_model_len, (batch_size, 1), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    seq_lens = context_lens - next_n + 1 + torch.arange(next_n, device="cuda")
+    seq_lens = seq_lens.to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+
+    full_sms = get_num_sms()
+    decode = DeepSeekV32IndexerDecodeMetadata(
+        block_table=block_table,
+        seq_lens=seq_lens,
+        decode_lens=torch.full((batch_size,), next_n, device="cuda"),
+        requires_padding=False,
+        schedule_metadata=get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(seq_lens, block_size, full_sms),
+        schedule_num_sms=full_sms,
+        schedule_block_size=block_size,
+    )
+
+    def paged_mqa_logits(schedule_metadata: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(
+            (q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), None),
+            kv_cache,
+            weights,
+            seq_lens,
+            block_table,
+            schedule_metadata,
+            max_model_len,
+            clean_logits=False,
+        )
+
+    assert decode.get_schedule_metadata() is decode.schedule_metadata
+    ref_logits = paged_mqa_logits(decode.schedule_metadata)
+
+    # What `create_sm_control_context` does while DBO microbatches run.
+    set_num_sms(full_sms - 20)
+    try:
+        schedule_metadata = decode.get_schedule_metadata()
+        assert schedule_metadata is not decode.schedule_metadata
+        # Later indexer layers of the same forward reuse it.
+        assert decode.get_schedule_metadata() is schedule_metadata
+        logits = paged_mqa_logits(schedule_metadata)
+    finally:
+        set_num_sms(full_sms)
+    assert decode.get_schedule_metadata() is decode.schedule_metadata
+
+    # Columns past each row's context length are never written.
+    valid = torch.arange(max_model_len, device="cuda") < seq_lens.view(-1, 1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        logits.masked_fill(~valid, 0), ref_logits.masked_fill(~valid, 0)
+    )

why can not we build metadata based on `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` in the first place? Instead of changing it at forward time?

> why can not we build metadata based on `total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS` in the first place? Instead of changing it at forward time?

@zyongye  I considered that, so:
 - Whether a step is microbatched is only known per step, and the builder doesn't know. With --enable-dbo, DP ranks decide each step whether to split, and steps that don’t split run with all SMs. The microbatch-0 builder (get_metadata_builder(ubid or 0)) builds metadata for both split and unsplit steps, and build() gets no microbatch flag. A schedule planned for the reduced count up front would hit the same _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 assertion on every unsplit step. Doing it at build time would mean passing a “microbatched / compute SM count” argument from the runner into the builder, in both MRV1 and MRV2.
 
- The compute SM count actually isn’t just total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS. create_sm_control_context uses min(VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS, all2all_manager.max_sms_used()), forces 0 on ROCm with DeepEP HT, and only calls deep_gemm.set_num_sms when DeepGEMM is available and the comm SM count is > 0. The builder would need to duplicate that and stay in sync with it.

Re-planning at the call site uses the SM count DeepGEMM is actually running with (get_num_sms()), so it stays correct whichever code path changes it (The cost ofc is one small metadata kernel per microbatch, on the first indexer layer.)

> The microbatch-0 builder (get_metadata_builder(ubid or 0)) builds metadata for both split and unsplit steps, and build() gets no microbatch flag.
